n-k-k6-02.title: Which groups fit enter?
n-k-k6-02.topic: Read rules with limits: groups, ratios and budget
n-k-k6-02.goal: Read entrance notice where rules limit each other, build several groups meeting all at once, and explain why one kind no fit work.
n-k-k6-02.material:
Your club wan visit children science museum. Read notice and budget.

[어린이 과학관 단체 입장 안내]
- 요금: 어른 한 명 5,000원, 어린이 한 명 3,000원
- 어린이는 어른과 함께 와야 합니다. 어른 한 명당 어린이 세 명까지 들어갈 수 있습니다.
- 단체 입장은 모두 5명 이상일 때만 가능합니다.
- 어린이가 1명 이상 있는 단체만 신청할 수 있습니다.

Your club budget: 총 요금 25,000원 이하 (total fee at most 25,000 won).
n-k-k6-02.thinking.0: Turn Korean quantity words into conditions
n-k-k6-02.thinking.2: See how one rule limit another
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.prompt: Look only at adult/child rule (ignore price and group-size rules). Which visit not allowed?
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.hint.0: Read ‘어른 한 명당 어린이 세 명까지’ as rule for each adult separately.
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.hint.1: For each option, multiply adult number by allowed children and compare.
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.r.b: Allowed: one adult fit bring up to 3 children; 3 na limit itself.
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.r.c: Allowed: 2 adults fit bring up to 6 children.
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.r.d: Allowed: 4 adults fit bring up to 12 children.
n-k-k6-02.s.s1.explain: Limit na 3 children for EACH adult. Two adults fit bring maximum 2 x 3 = 6 children, so 7 too many.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.prompt: Build 3 groups wey meet EVERY rule and budget. a = adults, c = children.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.hint.0: Write 4 conditions in your own words first (adults, children per adult, total people, cost).
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.hint.1: Choose adult count first, then find child counts allowed by ratio rule and 5-person minimum.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.hint.2: Check money last: 5,000 x adults + 3,000 x children.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.fail.c0: Use whole people counts (children 0 or more).
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.fail.c1: 어린이는 어른과 함께 와야 합니다: at least one adult.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.ok.c2: No more than 3 children for each adult.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.fail.c2: Too many children: max 3 for each adult.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.fail.c3: 단체 입장은 5명 이상: 5 or more people total.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.fail.c5: 어린이가 1명 이상 있는 단체만 신청할 수 있습니다: at least one child.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.explain: For example, 2 adults + 3 children = 19,000 won; 3 + 2 = 21,000 won; 4 + 1 = 23,000 won. Six groups fit total: (2,3), (2,4), (2,5), (3,2), (3,3), (4,1). Notice give limits, no be one exact group.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.because.prompt: Try group with exactly ONE adult. In one or two sentences (English or Korean), explain why no group like that fit all rules. Use numbers.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.because.hint.0: Count maximum number of people group with one adult fit have.
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: I use 3-children limit and 5-person minimum together?
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: My numbers also work for 2 adults?
n-k-k6-02.s.s2.because.model.1: With 1 adult, max 3 children fit come, so group only 4 people, but minimum na 5.

n-k-k6-05.s.s1.prompt: Read each part, choose most likely interpretation and continue.
n-k-k6-05.title: He do homework?
n-k-k6-05.topic: Ambiguous message: 다 + 안 fit mean ‘none’ or ‘not all’
n-k-k6-05.goal: Read short exchange step by step, notice ‘ㅡ 다 안 했어요’ fit mean two things, change interpretation as details come, and write clear sentences.
n-k-k6-05.material: Teacher ask about homework. Homework get 10 questions.
n-k-k6-05.thinking.0: Hold two meanings of one sentence
n-k-k6-05.thinking.1: Change reading when new details arrive
n-k-k6-05.thinking.2: Reword message so nobody misread am
n-k-k6-05.prereq.0: Know 안 + verb and 못 + verb
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.hint.0: Use only what you read so far, and say every meaning sentence fit get.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.hint.1: Ask which meanings still fit after new lines appear.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.0.after: Both meanings fit: ‘다 안 했어요’ fit mean ‘did none’ or ‘did not do all.’ ‘죄송해요’ show something missing, but not how much.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.0.o.b: He did some, but never finish.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.0.r.c: He say 죄송해요, so something missing; that no fit if he finish all.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.0.o.d: He do homework for another class.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.1.ask: Now wetin ‘숙제를 다 안 했어요’ mean?
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.1.after: Details settle am: he do 8 of 10, so sentence mean ‘not all.’
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.1.r.a: He say he do questions 1 to 8.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.1.o.b: He do most and miss last 2.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.1.r.d: His second answer say exactly which questions he do.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.2.ask: Which sentence should 유나 write so teacher no mistake am for ‘did most’?
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.2.after: ‘하나도 안 했어요’ mean none. ‘다는 못 했어요’ clearer way to say ‘not all.’
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This same ambiguous sentence again; e no rule out ‘did some.’
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.2.r.c: This sound like ‘did some but not all,’ opposite of wetin 유나 want to say.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.st.2.r.d: This say she do almost all.
n-k-k6-05.s.s1.reflect: Notice same words remain, only details change your interpretation. Speaker wey want clarity suppose use words with one meaning.
n-k-k6-05.s.s2.prompt: Which sentence fit confuse people same way as ‘숙제를 다 안 했어요’?
n-k-k6-05.s.s2.hint.0: Find sentence with word meaning ‘all’ plus negative.
n-k-k6-05.s.s2.hint.1: Try each sentence in two different situations and see which fit both.
n-k-k6-05.s.s2.r.b: This say guests never arrive yet; no ‘all or none’ split.
n-k-k6-05.s.s2.r.d: This say few came; no ‘none or not all’ ambiguity.
n-k-k6-05.s.s2.explain: ‘다’ (all) followed by negative fit mean ‘none’ or ‘not all,’ so ‘손님이 다 안 왔어요’ get same two meanings.
n-k-k6-05.s.s3.prompt: Write two polite Korean sentences about DIFFERENT tasks (e.g. homework, cleaning, book). Sentence 1: you do none of first task. Sentence 2: you do part of second task. Do not use ‘다 안’ or ‘다 못’ in either.
n-k-k6-05.s.s3.hint.0: For ‘none,’ choose word wey mean ‘not even one.’
n-k-k6-05.s.s3.hint.1: For ‘part,’ say how much you do (half, small amount, up to a point) or use form wey mean ‘not all.’
n-k-k6-05.s.s3.selfAssess.0: Each sentence fit only one meaning?
n-k-k6-05.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Two sentences really talk about different amounts?

n-k-k6-04.title: Summary match report?

[학교 신문: 급식 설문 결과]

n-k-k6-04.thinking.1: Check wetin each claim based on

n-k-k6-04.prereq.1: Fit read short report and relayed speech (-대 / -래)
n-k-k6-04.s.s1.prompt: Compare 하준 summary with report. Choose one line NOT supported by report. (More than one wrong.)
n-k-k6-04.s.s1.hint.0: Read summary one line at a time and find report sentence it come from.
n-k-k6-04.s.s1.hint.1: For each line compare students report numbers cover with students line talk about.

n-k-k6-04.s.s2.r.a: Numbers 24 and 14 in summary same as report.
n-k-k6-04.s.s2.o.b: Something known about one class was said about bigger group.
n-k-k6-04.s.s2.o.c: Polite endings change to casual endings.
n-k-k6-04.s.s2.r.c: Casual endings normal in summary for friend, no content mistake.
n-k-k6-04.s.s2.o.d: Some survey results missing from summary.
n-k-k6-04.s.s2.r.d: Wrong lines add claims; dem no drop results.
n-k-k6-04.s.s2.explain: Report about 24 students in one class. Wrong lines stretch result to all sixth graders, other classes or whole school, wey report never say.
n-k-k6-04.s.s3.prompt: Rewrite last summary line (about not leaving food) so e say only wetin report say (casual to friend fine).

n-k-k6-01.title: Read numbers from library

n-k-k6-01.goal: Decide which statements small library number table support, find gap between poster headline and table, and explain with number.
n-k-k6-01.material:
Neighbourhood library show table and poster.

[우리 동네 도서관 3월 이용 현황]

이용자 수 | 2,400명 | 3,000명

n-k-k6-01.s.s1.prompt: Which statements table itself support, no guessing? Choose all.
n-k-k6-01.s.s1.hint.0: Mark each statement ‘number I can point to’ or ‘something I need to guess.’
n-k-k6-01.s.s1.hint.1: For number claims, find two figures and compare in right direction.
n-k-k6-01.s.s1.r.a: Liking books na feeling; table count visits and borrowed books, no feeling.
n-k-k6-01.s.s1.r.c: Compare 5,200 and 5,100 again: borrowed books number go the other way.
n-k-k6-01.s.s1.r.d: Table mention study room only in side note; e no show say room cause increase.

n-k-k6-01.s.s2.prompt: Wetin be main gap between poster headline and table?

n-k-k6-01.s.s2.o.d: Poster talk about reading, but table count visits and loans, and loans no rise.

n-k-k6-01.s.s3.prompt: In 1-2 sentences (English or Korean), say whether table support poster headline and why. Use at least one number.
n-k-k6-01.s.s3.hint.0: Name table row closest to ‘reading’ and give two numbers.
n-k-k6-01.s.s3.hint.1: Then say wetin that row no show about headline.

n-k-k6-01.s.s3.model.0: Table show visitors rise (2,400 to 3,000), but books borrowed drop from 5,200 to 5,100, so e no show say people read more.

n-k-k6-03.title: Is coupon enough to decide?
